procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks after a 32-week cesarean delivery for preterm labor. The baby came home from the NICU on January 6 and is feeding and growing; follow-up with neonatal clinic is set. She saw OB last week, incision healed, cleared for normal activity.

How she is doing: tired, up at night, but says the worst stretch was the NICU weeks. Appetite fine. No heavy bleeding now. Some low mood on the hard days, no anhedonia, no thoughts of harming herself or the baby. Husband home in the evenings, her mother helping two days a week.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with DHA daily, continuing while nursing. Levocetirizine off season.

Exam: vitals in chart. Appears well, tired. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Low transverse incision well healed, no tenderness. No calf tenderness or leg swelling.

PHQ-9 4.

A/P:
1. Postpartum after preterm cesarean delivery: recovering well. CBC and TSH today.
2. History of preterm labor now on her problem list; in a future pregnancy she should be seen early by OB. She is not thinking about that yet.
3. Mood: mild fatigue-related symptoms, normal range score. Talked about warning signs and that she can text me directly. Recheck at her physical.
4. Surgical history updated: low transverse cesarean 12/2024.

documents.title: Bloodwork
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count has recovered nicely after the delivery and your thyroid level is normal. Nothing to do. Give the little one a cuddle from all of us.

documents.title: Allergy pill while nursing?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pollen is back. Is it OK to take my levocetirizine again while I'm still breastfeeding? Same 5 mg as usual.

documents.title: RE: Allergy pill while nursing?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, fine to restart your usual 5 mg once a day at bedtime. Watch the baby for unusual sleepiness, which is uncommon at that dose. If it's not enough, let me know.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx renewal request, prenatal vitamin with DHA, 90-day. Patient still taking daily. Renewed per protocol, 3 refills.

events.reason: shortness of breath and dry cough after high-altitude hiking

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Patchy bilateral alveolar opacities, most evident in the mid and lower lung zones. Heart size normal. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Osseous structures intact.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral alveolar infiltrates; in the setting of recent ascent, consistent with high-altitude pulmonary edema.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD (outside hospital)
Date of service: 7/21/2025, with overnight observation to 7/22/2025
Patient: Delaney Martel, 33F

CC: getting more short of breath with a dry cough since a hiking trip.

HPI: Flew home this afternoon from a backpacking trip in the Rocky Mountains. Over two days the group climbed to about 12,000 feet. Breathlessness started on the second day up and has worsened since, now with minimal exertion, plus a nonproductive cough. No sick contacts, no recent illness before the trip, no fever, chest pain, leg swelling or hemoptysis. Delivered a baby by cesarean in late 2024 after preterm labor; otherwise healthy apart from seasonal allergies.
Meds: levocetirizine 5 mg seasonal, prenatal vitamin with DHA.
Allergies: latex (rash), penicillin.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol, environmental consultant.
Family: maternal aunt with known susceptibility to high-altitude pulmonary edema.

Triage: T 37.2 C (99 F), BP 130/80, HR 95, RR 26, SpO2 86% on room air; 94% on supplemental oxygen by nasal cannula.
Exam: tachypneic, speaking in full sentences on oxygen. Crackles at both lung bases. Heart regular, no murmur. No JVD. Calves soft and nontender, no edema.

Results: WBC 11.0, hemoglobin 14.5, platelets 250. Procalcitonin 0.1 ng/mL (reference under 0.5). Basic metabolic panel normal. Urine hCG negative. Room-air arterial gas: pH 7.45, PaCO2 30, PaO2 55, HCO3 24.
Chest x-ray: bilateral alveolar infiltrates, normal heart size.

MDM: Acute hypoxemia with bilateral infiltrates after rapid ascent, low procalcitonin and no infectious prodrome; picture fits high-altitude pulmonary edema, now at low altitude. Placed in observation on nasal cannula oxygen.

Observation course: oxygen weaned overnight. Morning SpO2 95% on room air at rest, HR 78, RR 16. Cough easing. Walked the hall without desaturation below 94%.

Disposition: discharged home 7/22. Diagnosis: high-altitude pulmonary edema with hypoxemia, resolving. Advised slow, staged ascent for any future high-altitude travel and to discuss prevention with her PCP before such a trip. Follow up with PCP within a week. Return for worsening breathing.

Emergency physician

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen a week after an ED visit and one night of observation for high-altitude pulmonary edema; ED record reviewed (room-air sat 86%, PaO2 55, bilateral infiltrates, procalcitonin 0.1). First trip back to the mountains since the baby. She went from low altitude to about 12,000 ft over two days.

Now: breathing back to normal by Thursday. Cough gone. Back to walking with the stroller, no breathlessness on the hill by her house. No fever, chest pain or leg swelling.

Exam: comfortable. Room-air sat normal at rest and after a lap of the hallway. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P: High-altitude pulmonary edema, clinically resolved at sea level.
- Repeat 2-view chest film in about 4 weeks to document clearing.
- Talked about why the maternal aunt's history matters: she is likely susceptible and at risk of recurrence. Any future trip above about 8,000 ft should be a slow ascent with rest days, and she should come see me well before going so we can make a plan. Descend at the first sign of breathlessness.
- Otherwise continue prenatal vitamin, levocetirizine in season.

reports.text: Comparison: outside chest radiograph 7/21/2025. PA and lateral views. The previously described bilateral alveolar opacities have cleared. Lungs are clear. Heart and mediastinum normal in size and contour. No effusion or pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Clear lungs. Interval resolution of prior bilateral opacities.

documents.title: Chest x-ray
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your chest x-ray yesterday is completely clear; the fluid seen in July is gone. I'm marking the altitude episode as resolved. The plan for any future mountain trip still stands: check in with me beforehand.

documents.title: RE: Chest x-ray
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great news, thank you. No big climbs planned for a while.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.
reports.conclusion: NILM, high-risk HPV negative. Routine screening in 5 years.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33F for her yearly physical. Busy with work and a baby who is now crawling everywhere. Stopped nursing in September. Breathing has been fine since the summer episode. Allergy season was ordinary.

They hope to try for a second pregnancy in the coming months. Reviewed: history of preterm labor and a cesarean in Dec 2024, so she should message us with a positive test right away and get to OB early; she would like to see maternal-fetal medicine as well. Still on prenatal vitamin with DHA, which is the right thing.

Interval history: ED visit and observation 7/2025 for high-altitude pulmonary edema, follow-up x-ray clear in August.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with DHA daily; levocetirizine 5 mg in season. Allergies: latex, penicillin.
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks a week, consultant work mostly from home now.

Exam: vitals in chart, weight back to her baseline. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear to bases. Abdomen soft, cesarean scar well healed. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV collected. Extremities no edema. Skin normal.

Plan:
- Pap/HPV sent (last 2020).
- CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c.
- PHQ-2 1.
- Flu and 2025-26 COVID vaccines today, latex-free.
- Message with a positive pregnancy test.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap smear and HPV test were both normal, so you're set for five years. Bloodwork from Monday was all normal too. Talk soon.

documents.title: Pregnant again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Positive test this morning! LMP was December 4. You said to tell you right away. Can we do the referral to OB and MFM?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant again
documents.author: RN
documents.body: That's wonderful news. We have a nurse slot Wednesday at 8 to confirm and send both referrals the same day.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Urine hCG positive, about 5 1/2 weeks by LMP 12/4/25. No bleeding or pain. Taking prenatal vitamin. PCP reviewed: referral to her prior obstetrics group with request for maternal-fetal medicine involvement given preterm labor at 32 weeks and a cesarean 13 months ago. Pregnancy added to the problem list.

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-Fetal Medicine consultation, visit 2/10/2026
Re: Delaney Martel, 33, G2P0101

Reason: early consultation for a pregnancy after spontaneous preterm labor with delivery at 32 weeks (12/2024, low transverse cesarean, breech).

Current pregnancy: 9 weeks 5 days by LMP, confirmed by ultrasound with a single live intrauterine pregnancy and a normal heart rate. Feels well. Prenatal labs ordered with her obstetrician and returned normal.

Other history: seasonal allergic rhinitis; high-altitude pulmonary edema 7/2025, resolved. Allergies: latex (rash), penicillin. Medications: prenatal vitamin with DHA, levocetirizine seasonally.

Recommendations: continue care with her obstetrician with MFM co-management; serial cervical length ultrasounds through mid-pregnancy; anatomy survey at 20 weeks here. Delivery planning to be discussed later in pregnancy.

Maternal-fetal medicine

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Renewal request from pharmacy for prenatal vitamin with DHA. Last filled January. Renewed, 90 tabs x 3.

documents.title: Maternal-Fetal Medicine Ultrasound Letter
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
MFM ultrasound, 4/14/2026, 18 weeks 5 days.

Single live fetus, growth appropriate for dates. Cervical length normal. Placenta anterior, away from the internal os and the prior incision. Normal amniotic fluid. Early anatomy views normal; full survey at 20 weeks.

Pregnancy uncomplicated to date. Continue routine prenatal care with obstetrics and cervical length surveillance.

Maternal-fetal medicine

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 weeks 1 day. Wanted to come in about her allergies and to catch up.

Allergies: usual spring symptoms, sneezing and itchy eyes on field days. Back on levocetirizine 5 mg at bedtime for two weeks with good control; OB and MFM are fine with it. No wheeze, no breathlessness, no cough.

Pregnancy: followed by OB with MFM. Cervical length checks normal so far and the anatomy scan is next week. Feeling movement. No contractions, bleeding or fluid. She is understandably anxious given last time but says the extra monitoring helps.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with DHA daily, levocetirizine 5 mg daily in season.

Exam: vitals in chart, weight up as expected for 21 weeks. Nasal mucosa pale and swollen, clear drainage. Conjunctivae mildly injected. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Gravid abdomen, nontender. No edema.

A/P:
1. Seasonal allergic rhinitis: controlled, continue levocetirizine through the season.
2. Pregnancy with history of preterm labor: in OB and MFM care, uncomplicated so far. She knows to go straight to labor and delivery for contractions or fluid.
3. Flu and COVID vaccines will come through OB this fall.
She will keep me posted.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY (outside hospital)
Patient: Delaney Martel  DOB 5/16/1992
Admitted 7/30/2026 - Discharged 8/3/2026

Diagnoses: preterm labor at 34w0d; preterm delivery by repeat low transverse cesarean; history of preterm labor and prior cesarean (12/2024). Neonatal death.

History: G2P0101. Pregnancy co-managed with maternal-fetal medicine and uncomplicated until the night of 7/29-7/30, when she developed sudden regular contractions and came in. She was in active preterm labor on arrival.

Course: given the prior cesarean 20 months earlier and active labor, she underwent repeat low transverse cesarean delivery on 7/30 under spinal anesthesia, latex-free. Surgery uncomplicated. Postoperative recovery routine; afebrile, blood pressures normal, incision clean. Discharged on postoperative day 4.

Newborn: liveborn male. Placed under the radiant warmer with drying and tactile stimulation but remained in respiratory distress. Breath sounds were diminished on both sides with fine rales. Arterial blood gas showed hypoxemia with respiratory acidosis. Chest radiograph showed a diffuse reticulogranular, ground-glass pattern with air bronchograms, consistent with respiratory distress syndrome. He was intubated and admitted to the NICU for oxygen and full support. Despite all measures he had a respiratory arrest and died on 7/31/2026. Lung tissue was sent for histologic examination; the report will be reviewed with the family by the obstetric team.

The family met with the NICU and obstetric teams and with the hospital bereavement service before discharge.

Allergies: latex (rash); penicillin.
Medications at discharge: routine postoperative analgesia; prenatal vitamin with DHA; levocetirizine as needed.
Follow-up: obstetrics in 1-2 weeks for incision check and in 6 weeks; MFM follow-up to discuss findings and future pregnancy planning. Primary care physician copied.

Obstetric hospitalist

documents.title: Thinking of you
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Delaney, I received the hospital summary yesterday and I am so very sorry about your son. There is nothing you need to do for me right now. When and if you want to talk, by phone or in person, text me and I'll make the time that week. I'm thinking of you and your family.

documents.title: RE: Thinking of you
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. It means a lot. I'm not ready yet but I will reach out.
